title: China's 604m Canton Tower Pinches to a ~22m Waist | China Travel Expert
description:
Guangzhou's Canton Tower looks like a simple needle from a distance — but it's an hourglass. At 604 metres (a 450 m body plus a 150 m antenna) it was China's tallest structure when it opened in 2010, built for the Asian Games.

The trick is the twist: the engineers (Arup, with Information Based Architecture) rotated the tower's top ellipse 45° against its bottom one. Where those two rings cross, the lattice squeezes into a narrow 'waist' only about 22 metres across — which is why the locals nicknamed it 小蛮腰, the 'slim waist.' Stand underneath and you can see the steel tubes spiral as they rise.

🧭 Expert Tip: go up near sunset so you catch Guangzhou in daylight and then watch the Pearl River skyline light up from the observation decks.

广州塔高604米，塔身上下两个椭圆相对扭转45°，最窄处的「腰」只有约22米，所以被叫作「小蛮腰」，2010年建成。
